title: National Clean Air Programme, GRAP and Vehicle Norms

cards.b:
Delhi's winter smog makes air policy a yearly headline. Prelims asks about the NCAP, AQI categories, Bharat Stage norms and GRAP. Mains asks why the problem persists and which fixes work.

Learn the figures and the institutions: CPCB, CAQM and state boards.

Expect a table-style question linking AQI band, health effect and the GRAP stage that follows.

The National AQI was launched in 2014 by the Government of India. It has six categories: Good (0-50), Satisfactory (51-100), Moderate (101-200), Poor (201-300), Very Poor (301-400) and Severe (401-500). It measures eight pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and Pb.

The CPCB runs the National Air Monitoring Programme. SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting) is run by IITM Pune and the IMD for big cities.

The National Clean Air Programme was launched in January 2019. It is a time-bound, national-level plan. Original target: cut PM2.5 and PM10 by 20 to 30 percent by 2024 against 2017 levels. It was later raised to a 40 percent cut by 2025-26.

It covers 131 non-attainment cities that failed the national standard for five years. The PRANA portal tracks progress. Funds go through the 15th Finance Commission grants for million-plus cities. It is not legally binding.

Bharat Stage (BS) norms are emission standards for engines, copied from the European model. BS-I started in 2000. India skipped BS-V and moved from BS-IV to BS-VI on 1 April 2020, a leap that cut sulphur in fuel to 10 ppm. The next steps include the shift to E20 petrol, CNG buses in Delhi (after the Supreme Court order of 1998 in M.C. Mehta) and a push to electric vehicles.

Vehicle scrappage policy (2021) removes old, polluting cars.

GRAP is an emergency plan for Delhi-NCR, first notified in 2017 on the Supreme Court's direction. Actions escalate with air quality:

  • Stage I (Poor): dust control, bans on burning waste.
  • Stage II (Very Poor): more parking fees, fewer diesel generators.
  • Stage III (Severe): halts on some construction, limits on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel vehicles.
  • Stage IV (Severe plus): truck entry ban, schools may go online.

The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) is the NCR body under the 2021 Act and runs GRAP.

Main sources in Delhi: vehicles, road dust, industry, power plants, construction and, in October-November, stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana. Winter inversion traps the pollutants close to the ground. Other sources: burning of waste, biomass cooking and diesel generators.

Ambient limits: the 2021 WHO guideline is 5 µg/m3 for annual PM2.5. The Indian standard is 40 µg/m3. The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1981 is the base law.

NCAP is not legally binding. Funds are often spent on road sweepers and not on source control. Many cities have too few monitors. The Delhi odd-even rule is cited as a short-term fix with small effect. Stubble burning needs farmer incentives for the Happy Seeder, biomass uses and crop shifts.

Some argue the focus should shift to regional airsheds rather than city boundaries.

Air pollution is a leading risk factor for early death in India. Studies in the Lancet put deaths in the lakhs per year. Smaller cities like Byrnihat (Meghalaya) and Ghaziabad often top the list. The Ujjwala Yojana (2016) cuts indoor smoke, and PM Surya Ghar and EVs target outdoor sources.

• AQI: 2014; six bands; eight pollutants.
  • NCAP: 2019; 131 cities; 20-30 percent, later 40 percent.
  • BS-VI: 1 April 2020.
  • GRAP: four stages; run by CAQM.
  • CAQM: statutory body since 2021.

Note also that PM2.5 are particles under 2.5 micrometres, which reach deep into the lungs and blood.

Prelims-style: "AQI includes which pollutants?" "BS-VI norms came into force in which year?" (2020).

Mains-style: "Why is air pollution in Delhi-NCR a recurring crisis? Evaluate NCAP." Structure: sources; health costs; NCAP and GRAP; gaps (non-binding, funds); way forward (airshed approach, public transport, stubble alternatives).

Use a number: the WHO annual PM2.5 limit of 5 against India's 40 shows how big the gap is.

quiz.q: The National AQI was launched in:
How many pollutants does the AQI measure?
quiz.w: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb.

quiz.q: How many non-attainment cities does NCAP target?
quiz.w: Cities that failed standards for five years.

quiz.q: India moved to BS-VI norms on:
Which body runs GRAP in NCR?
Which is the base law for air pollution in India?
quiz.w: It created pollution boards for air.

quiz.q: Which forecasting system is run by IITM Pune and IMD?
quiz.w: System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting.
